Problem_Classification.Algorithm: Block-wide binary (predicated) exclusive prefix sum (scan), implemented with a 3-phase warp-aggregated scan (Harris & Garland, Fermi-style)
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: For each element x in a per-block input array, compute the exclusive count of elements before it that satisfy a predicate (here valid(x) ≡ x > 0). Output[i] = number of valid elements in input[0..i-1]. This is the core "stream compaction / filter" primitive used to compute output indices for predicated writes.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. Each thread loads one int g_idata[threadIdx.x] and evaluates the predicate p = (x > 0). 2. (Phase A) binary_warp_scan: each warp uses __ballot_sync to obtain a 32-bit mask of predicates within the warp, then masks it with lanemask_lt() and applies __popc to obtain an exclusive intra-warp count (warpPrefix). 3. (Phase B) The last lane of each warp (laneIdx == 31) writes the inclusive warp total (warpPrefix + predicate) into sdata[warpIdx]; __syncthreads(). 4. (Phase C) The first warp (idx < 32) performs an exclusive Hillis-Steele warp_scan over the warp-partial totals stored in sdata[], using a doubled shared-memory buffer with zero-padded prefix to avoid branches; __syncthreads(). 5. (Phase D) Each thread adds its warp's exclusive partial total sdata[warpIdx] to its intra-warp prefix warpPrefix and stores the result to g_odata[threadIdx.x]. Host side: launches the kernel with grid = 12*7*8*9*10 = 60480 blocks of N threads each (N ∈ {32,64,128,256,512,1024}); every block redundantly scans the same N-element array (only threadIdx.x is used, not blockIdx.x) — this is a throughput micro-benchmark, not a full-array scan.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(N) work, O(log N) depth per block (warp scan = 5 shifts, partial scan = 5 shifts → total ≈ 2·log2(warpSize) = 10 sequential SHMEM rounds). Across the launched grid: O(grid_size · N) total work due to redundant blocks. Space: O(N) global I/O per block; O(2·(N/warpSize)) ints of shared memory per block (sdata[64] = 256 B fixed).

Bottleneck_Analysis.Classification: Mixed — primarily latency/occupancy-bound for small N (32–128); transitions to memory-bandwidth-bound for N ≥ 256 once the same 4·N-byte input is cached in L1/L2 and reused across all 60480 blocks. Effective arithmetic intensity vs. DRAM is artificially huge because of redundant reuse; vs. L1/L2 it remains low.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Per element (per thread): Global mem traffic: 4 B read + 4 B write = 8 B. Shared mem traffic: ~6 reads + 6 writes in warp_scan (only executed by first warp), 1 write in phase B (one lane/warp), 1 read in phase D → amortized ≈ 1–2 SHMEM ops/thread. Integer ops: predicate cmp (1), ballot (1), popc (1), 2 adds in phase D, plus addressing → ≈ 5–10 int-ops/thread. ⇒ AI ≈ 5–10 int-ops / 8 B ≈ 0.6–1.25 ops/byte against DRAM (first-touch). With redundant reuse across 60480 blocks reading the same N·4 B from L2: effective DRAM AI explodes (data is loaded once and reused), so the kernel actually runs against L1/L2 bandwidth, not HBM. Against on-chip caches AI is still ≈ 1 op/byte.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: RTX A6000 peak FP32 ≈ 38.7 TFLOP/s, peak DRAM BW ≈ 768 GB/s → FP32 ridge ≈ 50 FLOP/B. For 32-bit integer add throughput (~½ FP32 rate on GA10x, ≈ 19 TIOP/s), the INT ridge ≈ 25 ops/B. The kernel's ≈1 op/B is far below either ridge → Below ridge point → bandwidth/latency-limited, not compute-limited.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: For N = 32,64: occupancy / launch-and-sync latency — only 1–2 warps per block, __syncthreads() serializes phases, and small blocks cannot saturate 1536 threads/SM on GA10x. For N = 128–1024: shared-memory throughput in phase A's warp_scan and __syncthreads() barrier latency dominate; global memory becomes secondary because the 4·N B input fits in L1 (128 KB/SM) and is reused 60480× across the grid. No real DRAM-bandwidth pressure in this benchmark configuration.

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Streaming, perfectly unit-stride within a block (g_idata[threadIdx.x], g_odata[threadIdx.x]); cross-block: every block re-reads the identical N-element input (degenerate "broadcast" reuse).
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: 1:1 (one 4-byte load and one 4-byte store per thread in global memory).
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: Per-element global reuse within a single block: 1× (read once, written once). Effective grid-level reuse: 60480× (every block reads the same array — pathological reuse due to missing blockIdx.x indexing). Shared-memory reuse: sdata[warpIdx] is written once and read by all 32 threads in the warp = 32× reuse in SHMEM.
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Natural — consecutive threads access consecutive 4-byte words; one 128-byte sector per warp for both load and store.
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: Already block-tiled by construction (1 element/thread, 1 block = 1 tile of N elements). Shared memory footprint is tiny and fixed: sdata[64] = 256 B/block. Recommended tile = full block = up to 1024 threads. For real (non-benchmark) use over large arrays: have each block process T elements/thread (e.g., T = 4–8) with a thread-local sequential scan + one block scan of partials, reducing __syncthreads() cost and amortizing global load latency. Use cub::BlockScan or a 2-level (block + device) scan with carry-in for arrays larger than one block.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: 1 element per thread; 1 block scans N elements (N ∈ {32,64,128,256,512,1024}).
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Has RAW (prefix) dependency along the scan axis — resolved hierarchically: lock-step within a warp via __ballot_sync (warp-implicit sync), then across warps via shared memory + __syncthreads(); blocks are fully independent of each other.
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: Two __syncthreads() barriers per block (after phase B and after phase C); intra-warp synchronization via __ballot_sync(mask, p) (CUDA ≥ 9.0) implicitly synchronizes the participating lanes. No global atomics, no device-wide sync.
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: For GA10x (CC 8.6, max 1536 threads/SM, max 16 blocks/SM): 256 or 512 threads/block typically maximize occupancy (6 blocks × 256 = 1536, or 3 × 512 = 1536). N=1024 gives only 1 block/SM (1024/1536 = 67% occupancy). N=32 wastes the SM (need 16 concurrent blocks just to fill it, and the __syncthreads() per warp-sized block is wasteful). Theoretically optimal for this benchmark: 256 threads.

Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_Block: 48 KB default, opt-in up to 100 KB (49152 B / 102400 B)
Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_SM: 100 KB (102400 B) configurable unified L1/SHMEM out of 128 KB
Hardware_Constraints.Peak_Memory_Bandwidth: ≈ 768 GB/s (384 bit × 16 Gbps GDDR6 ÷ 8 = 768 GB/s; nvidia-smi reports 8001 MHz × 2 data-rate × 48 B/cycle)
Hardware_Constraints.GPU_Clock_Rate: 2100 MHz max SM clock (nvidia-smi); base ≈ 1455 MHz, boost ≈ 1800 MHz typical

Data_Shape.Input_Dimensions: 1-D arrays of length N, with N ∈ {32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024} (six independent benchmark instantiations via the bscan<N> template). Launched on a 1-D grid of 12·7·8·9·10 = 60480 blocks, each processing the same N elements.
Data_Shape.Data_Type: int32 (signed 32-bit integer) for both input and output; predicate is bool (x > 0).
Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Device buffers: d_in (N·4 B) + d_out (N·4 B) = 8·N B. N=32 → 256 B, N=64 → 512 B, N=128 → 1 KB, N=256 → 2 KB, N=512 → 4 KB, N=1024 → 8 KB. Host buffers (stack): h_in + h_out + ref_out = 12·N B (≤ 12 KB). Per-block shared memory: sdata[64] = 256 B (fixed regardless of N). All buffers fit comfortably in a single SM's L1 (128 KB) and in L2 (6 MB), which is why the 60480-block redundant grid behaves as an on-chip-cache benchmark rather than a DRAM benchmark.
